about: Each artist in DIRT has a plant in DRIFT's garden (build_soil_viewer.py, LIFE.garden): coleus leaves in the artist's colours (coleus: Plectranthus scutellarioides, whose leaves run the widest spectrum of any foliage), and a flower tied to the artist. 'tie' says how: work (they made or saved a work of it), process (it does what they did), form (it is the shape of their work), hour (it lives in the light they painted). Leaves are [vivid, dark, mid, rim]; the roster's artists take theirs from their palette unless given here. Flowers are [heart, petal, edge]. Forms: radial (petals round a heart), cluster (a dome of small florets), spike (florets up a stem), pitcher (a hollow), pad (a flower on a floating leaf). Every artist added to the roster gets an entry here (COWORKER.md, step 5).

plants.why: Meditative Rose (1958): a single red rose hanging in the sky over a plain.
Acanthus (Les Acanthes, 1953), one of the gouache cut-outs of his last years.
Its colour is soaked up from the ground it stands in (blue in acid soil, pink in alkaline), as her paint soaked into raw canvas. In DRIFT it is blue or pink by the colours of the soil under it.
It opens for a single night and is gone by morning: the decisive moment (Images à la sauvette, 1952). In DRIFT it stays open for a moment only.
Touch-me-not: its ripe pods burst and fling their seeds, as he flung paint. In DRIFT the seeds are thrown out in his colours when a flower falls.
Her Bacchus paintings of the late 1970s and early 1980s, the god among his vines.
Galaxy Apple, New York City (1964) and Apple Orchard, Tesuque, New Mexico (1981), both among Aries's saved works.
Flowers (1964): four hibiscus, flattened from a photograph by Patricia Caulfield and printed in every colour. In DRIFT each flower takes another.
The hawthorn blossom of The Arrival of Spring in Woldgate, East Yorkshire (2011) and his May-blossom paintings.
It opens at dusk, a yellow cup lit at the hour of his sunsets.
A hollow you look down into whose dark has no floor, as in Descent into Limbo (1992).
Still Life with Apples and a Pot of Primroses (about 1890), among Aries's saved works.
Irises (1889), painted in the garden of the asylum at Saint-Rémy in his first week there.
The Nymphéas of his pond at Giverny, painted for the last thirty years of his life.

Botanical Star on Stainless Background (2018), elasto plastic, paint and steel, among Aries's saved works: a star at once botanical and manufactured, as the wax plant's flowers are, stars within stars so regular they look moulded.

His flowers are faces, as in Face and Yellow Flower Head (1977), among Aries's saved works; a sunflower is a flower head, hundreds of florets packed in a golden spiral round one face that follows the sun.
Tulip Sunday (2015), a sugar-lift aquatint with drypoint, among Aries's saved works: tulips set out in a row as his Display Cakes (1963) are set out in a case.
